blocks.text: The hidden cost of your interview scheduling workflow

Your interview scheduling workflow is likely the single largest drain on your daily capacity. It is not one big project. It is hundreds of tiny tasks. You check an email. You open your calendar. You check the ATS. You reply to a candidate. You update the status. You notify the hiring manager. Each of these steps takes two minutes. When you do this fifty times a day, your focus is gone.

This is the scheduling tax. It feels invisible until you look at your screen at the end of the day. You realize you spent hours moving information between tabs. You are not alone in this. Most recruitment coordinators on Mac struggle with the same sprawl of browser windows. You have Gmail for communication, a browser-based ATS like Workable or JobAdder, and a calendar tool like Calendly open at once.
Using Lazur to manage your Mac workspace

Lazur helps you manage this complexity without leaving your current app. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on your screen. If you are lost in a complex ATS interface, ask Lazur where a specific button is. It draws a circle and a label around it. If you need to know how to perform a multi-step process, ask Lazur to guide you. It walks you through each click, one at a time, waiting for you to complete the step.

Communication is a massive part of your role. You send the same types of emails repeatedly. Scheduling requests, interview confirmations, and follow-ups. Instead of typing these from scratch, hold the fn key to dictate clean, formatted text directly into your email client. Lazur understands your context. You can say, 'Draft an email to the candidate confirming the interview for Tuesday at 2 PM with the hiring manager.' It puts the text at your cursor.
Always review the text Lazur drafts before you press send. Ensure the details match your company's communication style and follow all internal data privacy policies regarding candidate information.

items: 09:00: Ask Lazur to summarize your unread emails in Gmail to identify priority scheduling requests.
10:30: Use Lazur to guide you through updating a candidate status in your ATS when you forget the exact path.
13:00: Dictate notes into your interview scorecard in Notion after a quick debrief.
15:00: Ask Lazur to point at the correct calendar slot in your browser when you are looking at a crowded view.
16:30: Use Lazur to search for a specific document or policy on your company intranet while you stay in your messaging app.

blocks.text: Many coordinators try to keep too much in their head. They rely on memory for candidate status. This leads to errors. Another mistake is over-relying on manual entry. If you have an ATS that supports webhooks or integrations, use them. Use Lazur to help you navigate those settings once. Stop trying to remember where every setting lives in a deep sub-menu. Use the pointer capability to find it.

Do not ignore your keyboard shortcuts. If you use Gmail, learn the basic shortcuts. Pressing 'c' to compose is faster than clicking the button. If you are not sure what a shortcut is, ask Lazur to explain it. It will tell you the keys you need to press. This saves seconds on every single interaction. Over a week, those seconds turn into hours of saved time.

As a recruitment professional, you handle sensitive personal data. Always follow your employer's rules regarding candidate and employee information. Lazur does not store your screen content or audio after the request is processed. It does not train AI models on your data. However, you remain responsible for the content you send. Never ask Lazur to process information that violates your company's data handling policies.
What to do next for your workflow

Start by auditing your own time for one day. Note every time you have to leave your primary task to check a setting or search for information. These are your opportunities to use Lazur. When you find yourself clicking through the same three menus in your ATS, ask Lazur to guide you through it. When you find yourself typing the same email, use the dictation feature.

If you are ready to start, download Lazur and try it for three days. You do not need a credit card for the trial. See how it changes your interaction with your Mac. Focus on one app at a time. Start with Gmail, then move to your ATS. Once you feel comfortable, bring it into your daily Slack or Notion habits.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons in my ATS for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. It can point at buttons or guide you through a workflow step-by-step, but you must perform the actual clicks.

faq.question: Is Lazur safe for handling candidate data?
faq.answer: Lazur processes audio and screen data only while you hold the shortcut key. This data is not stored and is never used to train AI models. You should always follow your company's specific data privacy policies.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with all recruitment software?
faq.answer: Lazur works on your Mac, regardless of the app. It sees what you see on your screen. It works with any browser-based ATS like Workable, JobAdder, or Recruitee, as well as native apps like Slack or Notion.

faq.question: What happens if I forget how to do a task in my ATS?
faq.answer: You can ask Lazur how to do the task. It will provide a step-by-step guide on your screen, waiting for you to complete each action before moving to the next.
